title: Janaka's bow
hook: kings who couldn't lift it decided to take Mithila instead

segments.voice: Yesterday: Shiva's bow from Daksha's sacrifice, and Sita rising from the furrow. Your line was Sita rising from the furrow.

Janaka made a decision about his daughter, and he announced it. Sita, he said, is viryashulka: the price of her hand is strength. Not gold, not alliances, not land. Whoever can lift and string Shiva's bow may marry her. Word spread. Kings came from everywhere to try, and every one of them failed. Then, Janaka tells Vishvamitra, something ugly happened. Wounded pride doesn't always go home quietly. Sometimes it comes back with an army.
screen: `THE PRICE OF HER HAND: STRENGTH.` → `KINGS COME FROM EVERYWHERE.` → `EVERY ONE OF THEM FAILS.`

segments.voice: The kings who failed were furious, insulted by a bow. They joined forces and laid siege to Mithila. For a whole year the city was surrounded, and supplies ran low. Janaka, who couldn't match their armies, turned to austerity and prayer, and the gods answered him with an army of their own. The kings were scattered and fled. So when Janaka shows Rama the bow, it's no party trick. It's a test that has already cost his city a war, and he knows what happens when proud men fail it. If Rama can string this bow, Janaka says, I'll give him Sita. Then he orders it brought out, and Valmiki makes the scene huge. The bow lies in an iron chest on a cart with eight wheels, and the text says it takes five thousand tall, strong men to haul it in, with great effort. They set it down before the king and the guests. Think about what Rama is looking at. Not just weight. A bow a god once aimed at the gods. A line of kings who failed and turned to violence. A father who will give his daughter only for real strength. And the whole hall, waiting to see what the young prince will do.
screen: `VIRYASHULKA: STRENGTH AS BRIDE-PRICE.` · `THE KINGS FAIL, AND BESIEGE MITHILA.` · `THE GODS ANSWER JANAKA.` · `AN EIGHT-WHEELED CART, FIVE THOUSAND MEN.` · then, large: `THE HALL WAITS.`

segments.voice: Remember a time something didn't go your way in front of others, and the sting of pride that came with it, without flinching. Notice any urge, then or now, to blame the test or whoever set it; breathe it out, breathe in a little ease, and let the memory sit there, smaller.
Janaka's bow. The bow no king could lift, set as the price of Sita's hand, whose failure led proud kings to besiege Mithila for a year.
Your line: strength as the bride-price. The failed kings turned their hurt pride into a siege. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Across India, the contest of the bow is staged in Ramlila performances; later retellings such as the Ramcharitmanas present it as a swayamvara, while Valmiki describes Sita as viryashulka, won by strength.

fork.setup: you're Janaka. kings have failed your test and now surround your city. what do you do?
options: give Sita to the strongest of them.
turn to austerity and prayer, and keep your word.
break the bow so no one can try.
fork.reveal: he holds to his word and turns to tapas; the gods give him an army, and the kings are scattered.

original.note: Sanskrit vīryaśulkā: one whose bride-price is strength, vīrya (valor) + śulka (price).

trapdoor: what you thought: suitors came, failed, and that was that.
what it means: the failures led to a year-long siege; the bow is a test with a real cost.
what a scholar hears: Bala Kanda 66–67 call Sita viryashulka; the siege lasts a year and ends when the gods grant Janaka a fourfold army; the bow arrives in an iron casket on an eight-wheeled cart.

chat.says: Why was the bow such a big deal to Janaka by the time Rama arrived?
options: Failed kings had besieged Mithila over it for a year; the test had already cost a war.
It was the last thing his wife had left him, and he wanted it guarded.
He wanted to sell it, and needed a strong buyer who could carry it home.
chat.meaning: Kings who failed to string it laid siege to Mithila for a year, until the gods answered Janaka with an army.

viryashulka.meaning: a bride whose price is strength, not gold

Mithila.meaning: Janaka's city, besieged for a year by the failed kings

Shiva.meaning: the god who once raised this bow against the gods

Janaka.meaning: king of Mithila and Sita's father

recall: the monkey brother driven out by Vali

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 66 (viryashulka; the siege of Mithila)
Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 67 (the bow brought on its cart)

notes: Number of men hauling the cart: five thousand in the vulgate; confirm.
Swayamvara vs viryashulka: y1 day 38 already introduced the distinction; this day stays with viryashulka and the siege to avoid repeating it.
The gods' gift to Janaka: a fourfold army (chaturanga bala); confirm.
